items.title: A systematic review of nature-based solutions for climate action in African cities
items.title_en: A systematic review of nature-based solutions for climate action in African cities
items.title_zh: 关于非洲城市气候行动中基于自然的解决方案的系统性综述
items.summary_en: Nature-based solutions (NbS), including ecosystem-based adaptation, are increasingly proposed for climate action in African cities, but the evidence base is fragmented and lacks systematic synthesis of what is being implemented, where, and how effectively. We analysed 112 studies retained from a systematic review, covering 134 urban areas across 42 countries and including 45 informal settlements. Five NbS typology classes are inductively derived including: Green spaces; Rivers, catchments and drainage systems; Coastal systems; Green buildings; and Urban agriculture and multi-use gardens. Urban green spaces dominate the evidence (49% of studies) and are the most multi-functional class. Urban agriculture and multi-use gardens are under-recognised in headline framings, named as primary in only 5% of studies but appearing in 34% of the wider intervention mix. Evidence is increasing but concentrates geographically on larger cities. Successful climate change adaptation and mitigation outcomes are reported by 72% and 27% of studies, respectively. Heat mitigation is the most frequently quantified adaptation outcome, with temperature reductions up to 12.2 °C reported in proximity to urban green and blue spaces across the continent. Qualitative evidence links urban NbS to effective coastal protection, flood risk reduction, and increased water security. Multi-stakeholder governance anchored by local actors, and meaningful community participation are consistent enablers of effective implementation. However, insufficient long-term funding and livelihood disruptions and displacement raise concerns about long-term impacts. Priority research gaps include longitudinal effectiveness monitoring, financing mechanisms for informal contexts, systematic assessment of mechanisms behind inequitable outcomes, and evidence from under-represented regions and smaller cities.
items.summary_zh: 基于自然的解决方案（NbS），包括基于生态系统的适应措施，正越来越多地被提议用于非洲城市的气候行动，但相关证据基础较为零散，且缺乏对具体措施的实施情况、实施地点及有效性的系统性综述。 我们分析了从一项系统综述中筛选出的112项研究，这些研究覆盖了42个国家的134个城市区域，其中包括45个非正规定居点。通过归纳法，我们归纳出五类基于自然的解决方案类型，包括：绿地；河流、流域和排水系统；沿海系统；绿色建筑；以及城市农业和多功能花园。 城市绿地在证据中占据主导地位（占研究的49%），也是功能最多元的类别。城市农业和多功能花园在研究标题中未得到充分重视，仅在5%的研究中被列为主要内容，但在更广泛的干预组合中却占34%。 相关证据虽在增加，但地理上主要集中于大城市。72%的研究报告了成功的气候变化适应成果，27%的研究报告了减缓成果。热岛效应缓解是最常被量化的适应成果，据报告，在整个欧洲大陆的城市绿地和蓝地附近，温度降低了高达12.2 °C。 定性证据表明，城市基于自然的解决方案与有效的海岸保护、洪水风险降低以及水安全提升密切相关。以地方行为体为支柱的多利益相关方治理，以及有意义的社区参与，是有效实施的一致推动因素。然而，长期资金不足、生计中断和人口流离失所等问题，引发了人们对长期影响的担忧。 亟待填补的研究空白包括：纵向有效性监测、针对非正式环境的融资机制、对导致不平等结果的机制进行系统性评估，以及来自代表性不足的地区和小城市的实证数据。

items.title: Role of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in the extreme 2025 European summer heatwave
items.title_en: Role of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in the extreme 2025 European summer heatwave
items.title_zh: 大气环流和人为强迫在2025年欧洲极端夏季热浪中的作用
items.summary_en: In summer 2025, an extreme heatwave propagated –2025 record. However, the roles of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in the 2025 European high-temperature conditions remain unclear. Here we show that atmospheric circulation explains 82.5% (95% uncertainty interval: 65.0%–99.0%) and 51.9% (37.0%–65.2%) of the regional mean maximum temperature (Tmax) a–Baikal Corridor (BBC) patterns in SWEU, and BBC and Atlantic–Eurasia patterns in NEU. Detection and attribution using Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 simulations show that anthropogenic forcing increases the probability of exceeding the European mean June-July Tmax level observed in 2025 by a factor of 194.0 (95% confidence interval: 128.3–298.6). Greenhouse gas forcing increases the likelihood of exceeding this threshold, whereas anthropogenic aerosol forcing reduces it. These results provide insights into the roles of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in European high-temperature conditions.

items.title: Hot drought reshapes the relationship between tree species diversity and forest resilience
items.title_en: Hot drought reshapes the relationship between tree species diversity and forest resilience
items.title_zh: 高温干旱重塑了树种多样性与森林韧性之间的关系
items.summary_en: Climate warming is increasing the occurrence of hot droughts, in which water deficits coincide with anomalously high temperatures, posing growing risks to forest ecosystems and carbon sequestration. Yet whether tree species diversity (TSD) affects forest resilience differently under drought-only and hot drought remains unclear. Here, we conducted a global assessment of TSD effects on NDVI-based forest resilience following drought-only and hot drought events. By integrating satellite-based estimates of resilience with global tree species richness data and environmental factors across ten major forest biomes, we found that global forests exhibited reduced post-drought growth under both drought conditions, with more spatially extensive reductions under hot drought. Importantly, the TSD-resilience relationship differed markedly between the two drought types. TSD effects on forest resilience were widely negative under drought-only conditions but were predominantly positive under hot drought. Hot drought also amplified both positive and negative TSD effects relative to drought-only events. Interaction analyses further showed that, under drought-only conditions, TSD effects were broadly modulated by mean annual temperature and vapor pressure deficit, whereas under hot drought, mean annual temperature was the only environmental variable showing widespread modulation of TSD effects. In addition, resilience was more sensitive to the number of tree species under hot drought and in species-poor forests. Our findings highlight that anomalously high temperature accompanying drought reshapes both the direction and magnitude of TSD effects on forest resilience and identify low-richness regions as strategic targets where management interventions may deliver greater ecological benefits.
items.summary_zh: 气候变暖正导致高温干旱事件日益频繁，此类干旱中，水分短缺与异常高温同时出现，给森林生态系统和碳封存带来了日益加剧的风险。然而，在单纯干旱和高温干旱条件下，树种多样性（TSD）对森林韧性的影响是否存在差异，目前尚不明确。 在此，我们针对仅干旱和高温干旱事件后，树种多样性对基于NDVI的森林韧性的影响进行了全球性评估。 通过整合基于卫星的韧性估算值、全球树种丰富度数据以及十个主要森林生物群落的环境因素，我们发现，在全球范围内，两种干旱条件下森林的干旱后生长均有所减弱，而在高温干旱条件下，生长减弱的空间范围更为广泛。 重要的是，这两种干旱类型中树种多样性与森林韧性之间的关系存在显著差异。在仅干旱条件下，树种多样性对森林韧性的影响普遍为负，而在高温干旱条件下则主要为正。与仅干旱事件相比，高温干旱还放大了树种多样性的正负双重影响。 交互作用分析进一步表明，在仅干旱条件下，TSD效应总体上受年平均气温和水汽压缺口调节；而在高温干旱条件下，年平均气温是唯一对TSD效应产生广泛调节作用的环境变量。此外，在高温干旱条件下以及物种贫乏的森林中，森林韧性对树种数量更为敏感。 我们的研究结果强调，伴随干旱出现的异常高温会重塑温度-季节性差异（TSD）效应在森林韧性方面的方向和幅度，并指出物种丰富度较低的地区是战略重点区域，在此类地区采取管理干预措施可能带来更大的生态效益。
